data.long_meaning: Derived from the Old German word 'Got', meaning 'God'. Goetz is a name given to a person who serves as a pledge or hostage for God. In feudal societies, a goetz was a knight or vassal who pledged loyalty and service to a lord. The name Goetz carries the meaning “God's pledge or hostage” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Greek, Latin. Parents who choose Goetz usually hope their child will grow to embody god's pledge or hostage and live with faith, good character and purpose.
